name: FT230XS-R
title: USB 2.0 full-speed to basic UART bridge
summary: The FT230X is a single-chip bridge between a USB 2.0 full-speed port and a four-wire UART (TXD, RXD, RTS#, CTS#), running from 300 baud to 3 Mbaud. It needs no crystal: a 12 MHz internal oscillator and multiplier make its clocks, and 2048 bytes of MTP memory hold the USB descriptors, a factory-unique serial number and the setup of four CBUS pins. It runs from one 5 V or 3.3 V supply with I/O from 1.8 V to 3.3 V, detects USB dedicated charging ports, and comes in 16-pin SSOP (FT230XS) and 16-pin QFN (FT230XQ).
key_figures: 8 mA typ operating, 125 µA typ in USB suspend

notes: The suffix after the dash is the packing code: R reel, U tube (SSOP only), T tray (QFN only).

circuits.title: USB bus-powered configuration
circuits.description: The FT230X runs from the USB cable's 5 V. VBUS passes through a ferrite bead to VCC, which keeps noise from the chip off the cable; a 10 nF cap sits on the connector side of the bead. D- and D+ each go through 27 Ω to USBDM and USBDP, with 47 pF to ground on the connector side. VCCIO and RESET# are tied to 3V3OUT, so the I/O runs from the internal 3.3 V regulator, decoupled by 100 nF. VCC carries 100 nF and 4.7 µF.

parts.note: chosen for the total load current; Laird MI0805K601R-10 is one example

notes: The MTP power descriptors are set to the current the product draws.

USB rules for a bus-powered product: at most 100 mA at plug-in, at most 2.5 mA in suspend, at most 500 mA ever; a product over 100 mA uses a CBUS pin set to PWREN# to hold the plug-in and suspend limits, and cannot run from a bus-powered hub.

circuits.title: USB self-powered configuration
circuits.description: The FT230X runs from the product's own 3.3 V to 5.25 V supply on VCC and takes no current from the bus. Cable VBUS is divided by 4.7 kΩ and 10 kΩ into a CBUS pin set to VBUS_Sense. With the host off, VBUS_Sense is low, the chip stays suspended and the internal 1.5 kΩ pull-up on USBDP is not powered, so no current is pushed into an unpowered host. When the host powers up, the pull-up goes to 3.3 V and the host sees a full-speed device. VCCIO and RESET# tie to 3V3OUT.

parts.note: CBUS0 carries VBUS_Sense; any of CBUS0 to CBUS3 can be set to it

notes: The MTP power descriptor is set to zero (self powered).
While the FT230X is held in reset its UART pins are high impedance; the inputs drift high through their internal 75 kΩ pull-ups to VCCIO unless something drives them.

circuits.title: USB bus-powered with power switching
circuits.description: The bus-powered circuit with a high-side P-channel MOSFET that cuts 5 V to the rest of the product during USB suspend, so the whole product stays under the 2.5 mA suspend limit. CBUS3, set to PWREN#, drives the gate through 1 kΩ; 100 kΩ from source to gate holds the switch off when PWREN# is high. The 1 kΩ with the 0.1 µF from drain to gate slows turn-on: the switched rail rises at about 12.5 V/ms, reaching 5 V in about 400 µs, which keeps the inrush from resetting the FT230X or the host. A second 0.1 µF decouples the switched rail.

parts.note: chosen for the total load current; Laird MI0805K601R-10 is one example

notes: Without the soft start the turn-on surge can reset the FT230X or the host or hub controller.
A power switch IC with built-in soft start (Micrel MIC2025-2BM or equivalent) can replace the MOSFET.
In MTP, enable pull-down during suspend and assign PWREN# to one CBUS pin.
Logic on the switched rail needs its own reset when power returns after suspend.
A high-power product (100 mA to 500 mA) states its current in the Max Power field of the MTP memory.
PWREN# is powered from VCCIO; with 3.3 V logic, VCCIO stays on 3V3OUT rather than the switched rail.

circuits.title: USB to RS232 converter
circuits.description: The bus-powered front end with a 3.3 V TTL to RS232 line driver on the UART. TXD, RXD, RTS# and CTS# go to the driver, each pulled up to VCCIO by 10 kΩ, and the driver's RS232 side goes to a male DB9: TXDATA on pin 3, RXDATA on 2, RTS on 7, CTS on 8, ground on 5. CBUS0, set to SLEEP#, drives the driver's SHDN# so it drops to low quiescent current in USB suspend. CBUS1 and CBUS2, set to TXLED# and RXLED#, each sink an LED fed from VCCIO through 270 Ω.

parts.note: chosen for the total load current; Laird MI0805K601R-10 is one example
3.3 V TTL to RS232 with a SHDN# input; Zywyn ZT3243F (up to 1000k baud) is one example

circuits.title: USB to RS485 converter
circuits.description: The bus-powered front end with a ZT3485 transceiver on the UART. TXD drives the transceiver's driver input (pin 4) and its receiver output (pin 1) drives RXD. CBUS2, set to TXDEN, drives the driver enable (pin 3), so the driver is on only while a character goes out. CBUS3, set to PWREN#, drives the active-low receiver enable (pin 2), shutting the receiver off in USB suspend. RXD, TXD and TXDEN are pulled up to VCCIO by 10 kΩ, and PWREN# by another 10 kΩ. The two bus lines (pins 6 and 7) go to a male DB9; a 120 Ω resistor in series with a link terminates the cable when this node is at one of its ends.

parts.note: chosen for the total load current; Laird MI0805K601R-10 is one example
RS485 transceiver, 8-pin SOP, separate driver and receiver enables; Maxim and Analog Devices parts are equivalents
fitted when this node sits at an end of the cable

notes: The transceiver echoes what the FT230X sends back onto RXD; software removes it, or an OR gate combining TXDEN with the receiver output into RXD removes it in hardware.
TXDEN goes active one bit period before the start bit and inactive with the stop bit; this timing is fixed.

circuits.title: USB to RS422 converter
circuits.description: The bus-powered front end with two ZT3491 RS422 transceivers on the UART: one carries TXD (driver input, pin 5) and RXD (receiver output, pin 2), the other RTS# and CTS# the same way. SLEEP# drives both driver enables (pin 4, active high) and PWREN# both receiver enables (pin 3, active low), so drivers and receivers are on while the device is active and off in USB suspend. PWREN# has 10 kΩ to the transceiver supply Vcc; RXD, TXD, RTS# and CTS# each have a pull-up to VCCIO. The transceivers run from Vcc. Pins 9 and 10 are the differential driver outputs and 11 and 12 the receiver inputs; the cable connector carries TXDM, TXDP, RXDP, RXDM, RTSM, RTSP, CTSP, CTSM, ground and shield.

parts.note: SLEEP# on CBUS0 and PWREN# on CBUS1; any CBUS pin takes either option
RS422 transceiver for TXD and RXD; 2 RO, 3 RE#, 4 DE, 5 DI, 6 and 7 GND, 9 and 10 driver outputs, 11 and 12 receiver inputs
RS422 transceiver for RTS# and CTS#; same pins as U2
TXDM, TXDP, RXDP, RXDM, RTSM, RTSP, CTSP, CTSM, GND, SHIELD

notes: The ZT3491 handles up to 16 Mbaud; the FT230X sets the ceiling at 3 Mbaud.
In a bus-powered product a P-channel MOSFET switched by PWREN# in the transceivers' Vcc line may be needed to keep the product under the 2.5 mA suspend limit.

circuits.title: USB battery charging detection, one CBUS pin
circuits.description: The FT230X runs bus-powered from VBUS through a 600 Ω ferrite bead and powers an LTC4053 charger from the same VBUS. VCCIO and RESET# tie to 3V3OUT. The charger's BAT pin feeds the battery terminal block with 1 µF in series with 1 Ω to ground; the thermistor pin goes to the block's middle terminal and to a jumper that either biases it from VBUS through 4.32 kΩ (1-2) or grounds it (2-3, default). TIMER has 0.1 µF to ground and 2.2 kΩ pulls SHDN# low. The connector shell goes to SLD, with an unfitted 0 Ω to ground. CBUS0, set to BCD Charger, drives SHDN#: on a dedicated charging port the chip suspends with D+ and D- shorted, BCD goes high and the charger starts. 1.5 kΩ on PROG sets the charge current.

parts.note: battery charger; GND5 is pin 5 and GND11 is pin 11
VBUS 1, D- 2, D+ 3, ID 4, GND 5, shell lugs SHIELD

notes: Charge current: 1 A from a dedicated charging port, otherwise 0 A (enumerated, unenumerated and awake, or asleep).
MTP settings: CBUS0 set to BCD Charger; Battery Charger Enable set.

circuits.title: USB battery charging detection, two CBUS pins
circuits.description: The FT230X runs bus-powered from VBUS through a 600 Ω ferrite bead and powers an LTC4053 charger from the same VBUS. VCCIO and RESET# tie to 3V3OUT. The charger's BAT pin feeds the battery terminal block with 1 µF in series with 1 Ω to ground; the thermistor pin goes to the block's middle terminal and to a jumper that either biases it from VBUS through 4.32 kΩ (1-2) or grounds it (2-3, default). TIMER has 0.1 µF to ground and 2.2 kΩ pulls SHDN# low. The connector shell goes to SLD, with an unfitted 0 Ω to ground. CBUS2, set to SLEEP#, enables the charger through SHDN#. PROG has 16.5 kΩ to ground and 4.32 kΩ to CBUS1, set to PWREN#: when PWREN# is low after enumeration the two are in parallel and the charge current rises. The highest current is held to 0.4 A so a standard host is not overloaded.

parts.note: battery charger; GND5 is pin 5 and GND11 is pin 11
VBUS 1, D- 2, D+ 3, ID 4, GND 5, shell lugs SHIELD

circuits.title: USB battery charging detection, three CBUS pins
circuits.description: The FT230X runs bus-powered from VBUS through a 600 Ω ferrite bead and powers an LTC4053 charger from the same VBUS. VCCIO and RESET# tie to 3V3OUT. The charger's BAT pin feeds the battery terminal block with 1 µF in series with 1 Ω to ground; the thermistor pin goes to the block's middle terminal and to a jumper that either biases it from VBUS through 4.32 kΩ (1-2) or grounds it (2-3, default). TIMER has 0.1 µF to ground and 2.2 kΩ pulls SHDN# low. The connector shell goes to SLD, with an unfitted 0 Ω to ground. CBUS2, set to SLEEP#, enables the charger. PROG has 16.5 kΩ to ground, 4.32 kΩ to CBUS1 (PWREN#) and 1.5 kΩ to CBUS0 (BCD Charger#); each signal that goes low adds its resistor in parallel and raises the charge current.

circuits.title: Dual LED configuration
circuits.description: Two LEDs fed from VCCIO, each through 270 Ω, sunk by two CBUS pins: one set to TXLED# lights on transmit, the other set to RXLED# on receive. A pin pulls low from high impedance during traffic, stretched by a one-shot so short bursts still show.

parts.note: any two of CBUS0 to CBUS3; CBUS2 and CBUS1 carry TXLED# and RXLED# by default

circuits.title: Single LED configuration
circuits.description: One LED from VCCIO through 270 Ω into a CBUS pin set to TX&RXLED#, which lights on traffic in either direction.

equations.name: Baud rate

where.n: integer divisor, 2 to 16384; n = 1 with x = 0 is also allowed

equations.note: Divisors between 1 and 2 cannot be set. The reachable range is 183.1 baud to 3,000,000 baud; the driver works out the divisor from the requested rate (application note AN232B-05).

where.Res: equivalent resistance on the LTC4053 PROG pin

operation.text: A 12 MHz internal oscillator clocks the serial interface engine, protocol engine and FIFO controller and feeds a ×4 multiplier; the resulting 48 MHz, 24 MHz, 12 MHz and 6 MHz clocks serve the USB DPLL, the baud rate generator and the CBUS clock outputs. No crystal is fitted.

A 3.3 V LDO supplies the USB transceiver output stage, the 1.5 kΩ USBDP pull-up and the reset generator, and comes out on 3V3OUT with an external decoupling capacitor; it can also supply up to 50 mA to outside circuits. A 1.8 V LDO supplies the core. AVCC filtering is internal.

Full-speed transceiver with slew-controlled 3.3 V drivers, a differential receiver and two single-ended receivers for SE0 and USB reset; the 1.5 kΩ pull-up on USBDP is internal. The SIE does bit stuffing and CRC5/CRC16; the protocol engine answers chapter 9 requests and UART control commands. Compatible with UHCI, OHCI and EHCI host controllers. USB-IF test ID 40001463 (Rev D).

512-byte receive buffer holds data from the host's OUT endpoint on its way to the UART transmitter; 512-byte transmit buffer holds UART received data until the host reads it from the IN endpoint. RX and TX are named from the USB side.

7 or 8 data bits, 1 or 2 stop bits, odd, even, mark, space or no parity. RTS/CTS and XON/XOFF flow control are handled in hardware; RS232 BREAK is sent and detected. Each UART signal can be inverted and given high drive in the MTP memory. TXDEN can be routed to a CBUS pin for an RS485 driver. The baud rate generator divides 48 MHz with a 14-bit prescaler and 3 fraction bits into a 16× clock, from 183 baud to 3 Mbaud.

Outputs are 3.3 V CMOS and inputs TTL; the I/O runs down to 1.8 V on VCCIO with external pull-ups and the inputs tolerate 5 V. Drive strength is selectable from 4 mA to 16 mA. UART and CBUS inputs have internal pull-ups of about 75 kΩ to VCCIO, and can be set in MTP to pull gently low during USB suspend.

In asynchronous bit-bang mode TXD, RXD, RTS# and CTS# become a 4-bit I/O port written at a rate set by the baud prescaler, and the internal RD# and WR# strobes can be brought out on CBUS pins to clock external logic. In synchronous bit-bang mode the pins are read only when the device is written, so returned data lines up with the outputs (AN232R-01). CBUS bit-bang turns CBUS pins into GPIO.
An internal power-on reset needs nothing outside. RESET# lets external logic reset the chip; unused, it is tied to VCC or left open. In reset the UART pins are high impedance.

Runs from +3.3 V to +5.25 V with 8 mA nominal operating current and 125 µA nominal in USB suspend, below the 2.5 mA USB suspend limit. VCCIO from +1.8 V to +3.3 V sets the UART levels. With VCC at 3.3 V, 3V3OUT is joined to VCC and driven with 3.3 V.

When plugged into a USB dedicated charging port, which shorts D+ and D- and does not enumerate the device, the FT230X suspends and asserts BCD Charger (or BCD Charger#) on a CBUS pin so external logic can switch to charging. On a standard host the device enumerates, is not suspended, and the signal stays inactive. CBUS pins are set to these options with FT_PROG (application note AN_175).

After power-on or USB reset the chip reads its USB descriptors from MTP. The memory is programmed in circuit over USB with no extra voltage, using FT_PROG or D2XX calls. User areas hold application data, read and written over USB, within the 2,000 write-cycle rating. FTDI issues blocks of PIDs to users without their own VID (TN_100).
Free VCP (virtual COM port) and D2XX drivers, with no royalty, cover Windows (XP to 10, CE), Mac OS X, Linux and Android.
Top marking carries the part number, a manufacturing lot code and a date code YYWW (two-digit year, two-digit week) followed by the silicon revision letter.
